forecast-period.text: A low pressure system over central parts will move slowly east today. A ridge of high pressure will follow which will persist until Tuesday. On Wednesday a cold front moves over the south of the state, followed by another ridge of high pressure, with the centre of the high moving into the Bight on Thursday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and possible thunderstorms about about central and eastern districts, contracting east during the day. Maximum temperatures near to above average, grading to below average about the southeast. Fresh northeast to northwesterly winds about the east at first, tending fresh south to southwesterly about the west and extending throughout during the day.

Possible morning fog patches about central and western districts. Light showers about southern coasts. Maximum temperatures near to below average grading to above average in the west. Southeast to southwesterly winds.

Showers extending across the agricultural areas, with possible thunderstorms about the southern agricultural area. Maximum temperatures below average apart from in the northeast with maxima above average. Light winds tending northwesterly ahead of a fresh and gusty southwesterly change extending throughout the day.

text.p: Light morning showers about windward coast and ranges. Maximum temperatures below average grading to above average in the far west. Southwest to southeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: 1 to 5 mm about the northern agricultural area and south of the pastoral districts, increasing to 5 to 15 mm across the southern agricultural area, with possible falls of 15 to 30 mm about the ranges and the Lower South East district. Less than 2 mm about the far northeast.
